item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q006_ubiquitin_like_function_divergence","answer":"In the current public SCOPe 2.08 classification, ubiquitin-related proteins (family d.15.1.1; SUNID 54237), UBX domains (d.15.1.2; SUNID 54250), and Ras-binding domains/RBDs (d.15.1.5; SUNID 54263) are distinct families within the same Ubiquitin-like superfamily d.15.1 (SUNID 54236), beta-Grasp (ubiquitin-like) fold d.15 (SUNID 54235), and alpha-and-beta (a+b) class d. SCOPe explicitly treats the superfamily as a homology-bearing level, so this supports probable common ancestry and makes the conserved beta-grasp core useful for remote-homology recognition, domain-boundary assessment, and cautious structural-template selection. It does not establish shared molecular function: the separate families reflect substantial functional and interface divergence. It would therefore be unsafe to annotate a UBX or RBD as ubiquitin or a covalent ubiquitin-like modifier; infer ubiquitin-processing or E1/E2/E3-conjugation activity; transfer UBX-associated p97/VCP binding to ubiquitin-related proteins or RBDs; transfer Ras-family GTPase binding, partner specificity, or affinity from an RBD to the other families; or infer family-specific binding surfaces from fold similarity. Even within a named family, detailed function should not be assigned from SCOPe placement alone. Cross-family templates may support the core fold, but divergent loops and surfaces make them unreliable functional templates. Such assignments require independent family-specific sequence/orthology evidence, conservation of the relevant interface or catalytic/terminal features, and preferably complex structures plus direct biochemical binding or conjugation evidence.","evidence_used":["/api/v1","/api/v1/openapi.yaml","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ubiquitin&limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=UBX&limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Ras-binding&limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ubiquitin-like&limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d.15","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d.15.1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d.15.1.1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d.15.1.2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d.15.1.5","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ubiquitin-related&limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ubiquitin-related%20proteins&limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236/homology"]}]}
